analysis: The PR changes only documentation: CHANGELOG.md has historical context lines 1414-2008, and docs/architecture/inference.md adds a 'Model startup calibration' section plus code-map rows. It has no code, wire-protocol, key-handling, attestation or authorization changes. The docs describe provider-local startup/idle calibration (EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup, IdleCalibrationCoordinator, EngineV2.submitWithRetirement, ModelCalibrationPolicy). Calibration uses local-only one-token and 128-token warmups plus solo probes capped at 512 prompt and 32 output tokens. They run only while the Mac is idle, thermally nominal and outside Low Power Mode, and the docs say calibration yields no served-request or output-token counters. Documented evidence is published via existing capacity heartbeats. These are routing/capacity signals and not billing- or authorization-affecting per the docs, though the docs do not state that. Threat IDs touched: T-010 (the cancel/foreground-priority path, where beginForeground cancels probes), T-029 (idle GPU use) and T-007/T-027 (self-reported capacity trust). I found no concrete security regression. The code changes behind this doc (ProviderLoop+ModelCalibration.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration.swift, IdleCalibrationCoordinator) are outside this batch, so their enforcement was not reviewed. A later pass should check three things in that code: whether the probe prompts or KV stay out of the prefix cache (T-041, since the docs say 'uncached' probes), whether calibration data is never retained after retirement (T-028), and whether the heartbeat-reported rates are bounded and validated on the coordinator.
